2608.11753.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
2608.11753.paper_summary: Financial text is produced and interpreted within a market environment, yet financial text classifiers almost always receive text alone. We study whether financial time series are useful as an additional input on the task of classifying sentences from Federal Reserve communication as hawkish, dovish, or neutral. Our system, \lfts{}, extends the \lf{} architecture with this modality: a small voting network combines three independently trained components, a fine-tuned RoBERTa encoder, a prompted large language model (LLM), and a fused ensemble of time-series transformers over the market series of the months preceding publication. Because only about a thousand annotated sentences are available for training, the RoBERTa encoder is first pre-trained on sentences annotated automatically by the LLM and only then fine-tuned on the human labels. Trained on Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) communication up to 2015 and evaluated on 2015--2022, the fused system achieves 70.2\% weighted F1 -- against 64.1\% for the zero-shot LLM -- and overtakes it with as few as 240 human-labelled sentences. We take this as initial evidence for market time series as an input modality in financial text classification.
2608.11753.paper_summary_zh: 金融文本是在市場環境中產生和解釋的，然而金融文本分類器幾乎總是僅接收文本。我們研究金融時間序列是否作為額外輸入對於將聯邦儲備通信的句子分類為強硬、溫和或中立的任務有用。我們的系統，\lfts{}，擴展了\lf{}架構，加入了這種模式：一個小型投票網絡結合了三個獨立訓練的組件，一個微調過的RoBERTa編碼器、一個提示的大型語言模型（LLM），以及一個融合的時間序列Transformer集成，基於發佈前幾個月的市場系列。由於僅有約一千個標註句子可用於訓練，RoBERTa編碼器首先在由LLM自動標註的句子上進行預訓練，然後才在人工標籤上進行微調。該系統在2015年之前的聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）通信上進行訓練，並在2015年至2022年期間進行評估，融合系統達到了70.2\%的加權F1 -- 相較於零樣本LLM的64.1\% -- 並且在僅240個人工標註的句子下超越了它。我們將此視為市場時間序列作為金融文本分類輸入模式的初步證據。
